_README: The checked-in consumer map for lib/ doors whose SIGNATURE or MEANING changed,
enforced by tests/test_door_consumers.py. Keyed by FILE and CALL COUNT, never by
line number -- lines move on every edit and a line-keyed map would be stale before
Why this file exists: every unlisted consumer of a changed door is a defect of the
PLAN, not of a call site. When service_is_starting gained an optional second
argument (#1573 PR B) the two fleet-pulse call sites were missing from the first
draft of the plan -- and because the argument is OPTIONAL, nothing would have
broken loudly: fleet-pulse would simply never gain the marker rung, and on launchd
a queued bot would page session_missing AND service_down once per tick for its
whole admission wait. The boundary is greppable, so a test can own it.
A door leaves this file once every consumer has been migrated AND the door's old
shape is gone, not merely once the PR that changed it has merged.

service_is_starting.change: gained an optional [bot_dir] second argument; its first rung reads <bot_dir>/data/.boot-queued on BOTH OSes, ahead of the Linux-only systemd SubState rung. Every runtime consumer must pass a bot dir, and none may sit behind a `[ -n "$BOT_SERVICE" ] &&` short-circuit -- the marker rung needs no unit name, and gating on one made it unreachable for exactly the bots that have none.

lib/fleet-pulse.sh.why: the alerting side: the main loop's boot gate (session_missing / service_down) and the summary block's `starting` column. Two verdicts about one bot if they disagree.

lib/keepalive.sh.why: the healing side: the dead-session watchdog's SKIP. Restarting a boot in flight kills the very start that would have created the session (#1002).

lib/validate-bot-change.sh.why: bp_starting, the #1002 boot-window scenario's probe. Calls the door the way the fleet calls it so the scenario cannot pass against a signature production does not use.

tests/test_boot_admission.sh.why: the gate's own suite asks the predicate about a bot PARKED IN THE WAIT LOOP behind another bot holding the only slot — the one state no single-process test can reach, and the state the whole PR exists for.

tests/test_service_is_starting.py.why: the door's own suite drives it directly: once through the stubbed-unit-state harness (with and without a bot dir, on both forced platforms), and once immediately after a REAL boot_admission_acquire, which is what pins the marker format the gate writes against the parse this door does. A driver is exempt from the arity rule BECAUSE varying the arity is what it tests.

boot_rung_for.planned_change: #1573 PR C (F11) retires the composed systemd boot stagger; every reader of the rung moves with it.
boot_rung_for.note: Recorded here so PR C adds its row to this map rather than repeating the exercise. NOT enforced yet: the door is unchanged, so a map for it would fence a boundary nothing is moving.
